```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Wyska 2016 contributes two model files, both linked to this article:

* `Wyska_2016_lisofylline_mouse_pbpk` -- the fitted mouse model.
* `Wyska_2016_lisofylline_human_pbpk` -- the paper's projection of that model
  to a 70 kg adult.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_mouse_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description (mouse): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_mouse_pbpk"))$description`
* Description (human): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_human_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s13318-015-0260-y> (open access, PMC4954844)

Lisofylline (LSF) is the R-(-) enantiomer of the pentoxifylline metabolite M1.
The paper builds a flow-limited whole-body PBPK model from serum and six tissue
profiles in mice, then rescales organ volumes, blood flows and hepatic
intrinsic clearance to predict human serum and tissue profiles after a 3 mg/kg
10-min intravenous infusion and a 6 mg/kg oral dose.

# Population

Male Crl:CD-1 mice (8-10 weeks, 30.25 +/- 2.11 g) were fasted overnight and
given LSF 50 mg/kg into the tail vein. Groups of 3-4 mice were exsanguinated at
time points up to 60 min, and serum, brain, muscle, kidneys, liver, gut and
lungs were assayed by chiral HPLC-UV. The seven mean profiles were fitted
simultaneously in ADAPT II (maximum likelihood). The total number of animals is
not reported. Model physiology is for a 30 g mouse (Table 1 footnote b). The
human file has no fitted population: it is a 70 kg reference adult (Table 2).

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_mouse_pbpk"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment with its source. Summary:

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Brain, muscle, kidney, gut ODEs | n/a | Eqs. 1, 2, 3, 5 |
| Liver ODE (C_A x (Q_Li - Q_Gu) + gut outflow, MM metabolism) | n/a | Eq. 4 |
| Lung, remainder, arterial, venous ODEs | n/a | Eqs. 6, 7, 8, 9 |
| Residual error SD = sigma1 + sigma2 x Y | n/a | Eq. 10 |
| `v_<organ>` (mouse) | 0.50, 11.40, 0.50, 1.65, 1.50, 0.22, 13.05, 0.24, 0.94 mL | Table 1 |
| `q_<organ>` (mouse) | 0.47, 0.91, 1.27, 2.25, 1.50, 13.98, 7.58 mL/min | Table 1 |
| `lkp_<organ>` (both) | P = 0.345, 0.640, 0.777, 0.859, 0.892, 0.758 | Table 1 |
| `lvmax` | 9.644 ug/min | Table 3 |
| `lkm` | 1.777 ug/mL | Table 3 |
| `cl_renal` | 0 (fixed) | Table 3 |
| `fu` (mouse) | 0.76 | Methods, after Eq. 9 |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | 0.311 ug/mL, 0.250 | Table 3 (sigma1, sigma2) |
| `v_<organ>` (human) | 1400, 35000, 310, 1800, 1650, 1000, 24290, 1000, 3550 mL | Table 2 |
| `q_<organ>` (human) | 700, 750, 1240, 1450, 1100, 5600, 360 mL/min | Table 2 |
| `lclint` (human) | 1545.24 mL/min | Results text (Eq. 11) |
| `fu` (human) | 0.54 | Methods, after Eq. 12 |
| `lka`, `lfdepot` (human oral) | 0.024 1/min, 0.16 | Methods, after Eq. 13 |
| Oral input In(t) into venous blood | n/a | Eqs. 9 and 13 |

# Mouse: simulation of the 50 mg/kg IV bolus

The model is deterministic (fitted to mean profiles), so one typical animal is
simulated. The dose is 50 mg/kg x 0.030 kg = 1500 ug into the venous blood.

```{r mouse-sim}
mod_mouse <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_mouse_pbpk"))
ev_mouse <- rxode2::et(amt = 1500, cmt = "venous") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 60, by = 0.05)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L)
sim_mouse <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, ev_mouse, returnType = "data.frame"))

mouse_long <- sim_mouse |>
  dplyr::select(time, Serum = Cc, Brain = Cbrain, Muscle = Cmuscle, Liver = Cliver,
                Kidneys = Ckidney, Gut = Cgut, Lungs = Clung) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "conc")
```

## Figure 3: serum and tissue profiles

The published model curves of Figure 3 were digitised by the maintainers from the
article figure (points below); the lines are the packaged model.

```{r fig3}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~Serum, ~Brain, ~Muscle, ~Liver, ~Kidneys, ~Gut, ~Lungs,
  1,  83.6, 46.4,  20.9, 89.7,  84.5,  NA,   NA,
  4,  48.1, 17.6,  27.5, 50.6,  50.3,  50.4, 51.2,
  10, 30.7, 10.6,  25.5, 23.7,  24.1,  28.7, 31.1,
  20, 16.4, 5.67,  16.3, 11.1,  10.9,  15.2, 16.7,
  40, 3.96, 1.38,  4.86, 1.93,  1.91,  3.80, NA,
  50, 1.90, 0.681, 2.40, 0.822, 0.812, 1.83, 1.98,
  59, 0.956, 0.341, 1.26, 0.409, 0.390, 0.922, 1.02
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "published") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(published))

# the log axis cannot show the zero tissue concentrations at the dose time
ggplot(dplyr::filter(mouse_long, time >= 0.05), aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3, aes(time, published), colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~tissue, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Lisofylline (ug/mL or ug/g)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Wyska 2016. Red points: published model curves (digitised).")
```

```{r fig3-ratio}
fig3_cmp <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::left_join(mouse_long, by = c("time", "tissue")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = conc / published)
fig3_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(tissue, time, ratio) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tissue, values_from = ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (min)" = time) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Packaged model / digitised Figure 3 curve.")
```

The packaged model runs below the published curves: about 0.6-0.8 of them in
the first 10 min and about 0.35-0.65 at 60 min in every tissue except the
kidneys, which converge on the published curve late (see Assumptions and
deviations). The terminal serum half-life is close to the
published curve's, which is what the following check pins.

```{r fig3-check}
thalf <- function(t, c) log(2) / (-coef(lm(log(c) ~ t))[[2]])
sim_term <- sim_mouse |> dplyr::filter(time >= 40, time <= 59)
pub_term <- fig3 |> dplyr::filter(tissue == "Serum", time >= 40)
thalf_sim <- thalf(sim_term$time, sim_term$Cc)
thalf_pub <- thalf(pub_term$time, pub_term$published)
c(simulated = thalf_sim, published_curve = thalf_pub)
stopifnot(
  # Terminal serum half-life within 25% of the published curve.
  abs(thalf_sim / thalf_pub - 1) < 0.25,
  # The level gap is systematic, not a mis-transcribed parameter: every
  # tissue sits between 0.3x and 1x of the published curve.
  all(fig3_cmp$ratio > 0.3 & fig3_cmp$ratio < 1.05)
)
```

## Figure 4: arterial blood and remainder

```{r fig4}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~Arterial, ~Remainder,
  1,  73.4, 30.5,
  2,  50.6, 34.2,
  5,  31.2, 35.6,
  10, 22.7, 30.9,
  20, 14.6, 20.9,
  50, 3.44, 5.34,
  59, 2.18, 3.41
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "published")

fig4_sim <- sim_mouse |>
  dplyr::select(time, Arterial = Carterial, Remainder = Cother) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "tissue", values_to = "conc")

ggplot(dplyr::filter(fig4_sim, time >= 0.05), aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4, aes(time, published), colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~tissue, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Lisofylline (ug/mL or ug/g)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Wyska 2016. Red points: published curves (digitised).")
```

Figure 4 does not agree with Figure 3 of the same paper: its arterial curve
reaches 2.2 ug/mL at 59 min where the Figure 3 serum curve reaches 0.96 ug/mL,
and its terminal half-life is about 14 min against about 9 min, although the
text says arterial and venous concentrations are similar. No single
parameter set can reproduce both figures; the packaged model follows the
printed equations and Table 1 / Table 3 values, and sits closer to Figure 3.

## Closed-form checks of the reported clearances

The paper reports an intrinsic clearance of 5.427 mL/min and a well-stirred
hepatic clearance of 1.22 mL/min (Eq. 12, with fu 0.76 and blood-to-plasma
ratio 0.77). Both follow directly from the packaged values.

```{r mouse-clearance}
ini_m <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_mouse_pbpk"))$theta
clint_m <- exp(ini_m[["lvmax"]]) / exp(ini_m[["lkm"]])
ws <- function(q, fu, clint, bp = 0.77) q * fu * clint / (q + fu * clint / bp)
clh_m <- ws(ini_m[["q_liver"]], ini_m[["fu"]], clint_m)
c(CLint = clint_m, CLH = clh_m)
stopifnot(
  abs(clint_m / 5.427 - 1) < 1e-3,
  abs(clh_m / 1.22 - 1) < 5e-3
)
```

## Mass balance: the remainder-flow leak

Table 1 footnote a computes the remainder flow as the lung flow minus the sum
of all other flows *including the gut*, but the gut blood drains into the liver
(Eq. 4) and so already returns through the hepatic flow. Arterial outflow
(Q_Lu = 13.98 mL/min) therefore exceeds the flow delivered to the tissues
(12.48 mL/min) by Q_Gu = 1.5 mL/min, and the printed equations remove
Q_Gu x C_A from the body in addition to hepatic metabolism. The check below
confirms the packaged model reproduces that: the drug in all compartments plus
the cumulative metabolised and cumulative "leaked" amounts equals the dose.

```{r mass-balance}
states <- c("venous", "lung", "arterial", "brain", "muscle", "kidney", "liver", "gut", "other")
mb <- sim_mouse |>
  dplyr::arrange(time) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    body = rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(states))),
    leak_rate = 1.5 * Carterial,
    cum_metab = c(0, cumsum(diff(time) * (head(r_metab, -1) + tail(r_metab, -1)) / 2)),
    cum_leak = c(0, cumsum(diff(time) * (head(leak_rate, -1) + tail(leak_rate, -1)) / 2)),
    total = body + cum_metab + cum_leak
  )
mb |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(5, 15, 30, 60)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, body, cum_metab, cum_leak, total) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (min)" = time, "In body (ug)" = body, "Metabolised (ug)" = cum_metab,
                "Leaked Q_Gu x C_A (ug)" = cum_leak, "Sum (ug)" = total) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(max(abs(mb$total[mb$time > 0] / 1500 - 1)) < 0.01)
```

Over 60 min the leak carries away more drug than hepatic metabolism. It is
what lets the model clear the dose within the hour: with mass-conserving flows
(remainder flow 9.08 mL/min) the saturable hepatic pathway alone (at most
9.6 ug/min) leaves a 60-min serum concentration near 37 ug/mL, far from the
sub-1 ug/mL of Figure 3. The human projection of the paper (below) also only
reproduces the reported oral Tmax with the leak in place, so the packaged
models keep the equations as printed.

## PKNCA of the simulated mouse serum profile

```{r mouse-nca}
mouse_conc <- sim_mouse |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  # a single-subject solve returns no id column
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "50 mg/kg IV") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
mouse_dose <- ev_mouse |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "50 mg/kg IV")
nca_mouse <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(mouse_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(mouse_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
                         half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
))
nca_mouse_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_mouse) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
knitr::kable(nca_mouse_tab, digits = 3, caption = "PKNCA, simulated mouse serum (time in min, ug/mL).")
```

The paper reports a total clearance of 1.44 mL/min from a one-compartment fit
of the observed serum data. The packaged model's serum clearance (dose /
AUC0-inf) is about 1.9 mL/min, consistent with its lower concentrations
against Figure 3.

# Human projection

## Closed-form checks

Eq. 11 sums Vmax/KM over the four human-microsome pathways reported in the
Results (lisofylline-diol: KM 0.0230 and 4.23 mM with Vmax 0.0565 and
0.429 nmol/min/mg; pentoxifylline: KM 0.282 and 158 uM with Vmax 0.003 and
0.928 nmol/min/mg), scaled by 45 mg microsomal protein per g liver and a
1800 g liver. The paper reports 1,545.24 mL/min, and a well-stirred hepatic
plasma clearance of 477.54 mL/min (fu 0.54, blood-to-plasma 0.77).

```{r human-clearance}
# Vmax (nmol/min/mg) / KM (nmol/mL) = mL/min/mg protein
clint_mg <- 0.0565 / 23 + 0.429 / 4230 + 0.003 / 0.282 + 0.928 / 158
clint_eq11 <- clint_mg * 45 * 1800
ini_h <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_human_pbpk"))$theta
clh_h <- ws(ini_h[["q_liver"]], ini_h[["fu"]], exp(ini_h[["lclint"]]))
c(CLint_eq11 = clint_eq11, CLint_packaged = exp(ini_h[["lclint"]]), CLH = clh_h)
stopifnot(
  abs(clint_eq11 / 1545.24 - 1) < 2e-3,
  abs(clh_h / 477.54 - 1) < 1e-3
)
```

## Figure 5: 3 mg/kg IV infusion and 6 mg/kg oral

```{r human-sim}
mod_human <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wyska_2016_lisofylline_human_pbpk"))
dose_iv <- 3 * 70 * 1000   # ug
dose_po <- 6 * 70 * 1000   # ug
times_h <- seq(0, 150, by = 0.1)
ev_iv <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_iv, dur = 10, cmt = "venous") |>
  rxode2::et(times_h) |> as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "3 mg/kg IV (10 min)")
ev_po <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_po, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(times_h) |> as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 2L, treatment = "6 mg/kg oral")
ev_human <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_iv, ev_po)
# Two deterministic subjects: rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no
# omega, which is expected for this typical-value projection.
sim_human <- withCallingHandlers(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, ev_human, keep = "treatment",
                                returnType = "data.frame")),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)

human_long <- sim_human |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, time, Serum = Cc, Brain = Cbrain, Muscle = Cmuscle,
                Liver = Cliver, Kidneys = Ckidney, Gut = Cgut, Lungs = Clung) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(treatment, time), names_to = "tissue", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(conc_ng = 1000 * conc)

fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tissue,   ~time, ~published,
  "Serum",   5, 7670,  "Serum", 8, 8930,  "Serum", 15, 2600, "Serum", 45, 841,
  "Serum",   60, 653,  "Serum", 120, 363, "Serum", 148, 183,
  "Brain",   8, 3030,  "Brain", 15, 979,  "Brain", 30, 316,  "Brain", 60, 198,
  "Brain",   148, 65.3,
  "Liver",   10, 4940, "Liver", 15, 2490, "Liver", 30, 559,  "Liver", 60, 326,
  "Liver",   148, 109,
  "Kidneys", 10, 5410, "Kidneys", 15, 2700, "Kidneys", 30, 547, "Kidneys", 148, 113,
  "Gut",     10, 8120, "Gut", 15, 3310,   "Gut", 30, 873,    "Gut", 60, 541,
  "Gut",     148, 168,
  "Lungs",   8, 6600,  "Lungs", 15, 2020, "Lungs", 30, 674,  "Lungs", 60, 427,
  "Lungs",   148, 139,
  "Muscle",  10, 1290, "Muscle", 15, 1580, "Muscle", 30, 1320, "Muscle", 59, 759
)

ggplot(dplyr::filter(human_long, conc_ng >= 1), aes(time, conc_ng, linetype = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig5, aes(time, published), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~tissue, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Lisofylline (ng/mL or ng/g)", linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Wyska 2016. Red points: published IV curves (digitised).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig5-ratio}
fig5_cmp <- fig5 |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    human_long |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "3 mg/kg IV (10 min)"),
    by = c("tissue", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = conc_ng / published)
fig5_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(tissue) |>
  dplyr::summarise(min_ratio = min(ratio), median_ratio = median(ratio), max_ratio = max(ratio)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Tissue" = tissue, "Min" = min_ratio, "Median" = median_ratio, "Max" = max_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Packaged model / digitised Figure 5 IV curve.")
stopifnot(all(fig5_cmp$ratio > 0.3 & fig5_cmp$ratio < 1.2))
```

As in the mouse, the packaged human projection sits close to the published
curves at the end of the infusion and about half of them in the terminal phase,
with the same terminal slope.

## PKNCA and the reported oral Cmax / Tmax

The paper reports the simulated oral 6 mg/kg profile (mouse-derived ka and F)
as Cmax 572.12 ng/mL at 10.6 min.

```{r human-nca}
human_conc <- sim_human |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
human_dose <- ev_human |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)
nca_human <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(human_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(human_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

published_po <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~cmax,   ~tmax,
  "6 mg/kg oral", 0.57212, 10.6
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_human,
  reference = published_po,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "min", aucinf.obs = "min*ug/mL", half.life = "min"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published (Results text). * differs by >20%.")

po_res <- as.data.frame(nca_human) |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "6 mg/kg oral")
cmax_po <- po_res$PPORRES[po_res$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]
tmax_po <- po_res$PPORRES[po_res$PPTESTCD == "tmax"]
stopifnot(
  abs(cmax_po / 0.57212 - 1) < 0.2,
  abs(tmax_po - 10.6) < 3
)
```

The simulated oral Cmax is about 12% below the reported 572 ng/mL and Tmax is
about 1 min earlier. With mass-conserving flows the oral Tmax would move to
about 36 min, which is why the remainder-flow leak is retained.

The paper also projects the human hepatic clearance by blood-flow scaling of
the mouse value, 766.89 mL/min. With the reported mouse CLH of 1.22 mL/min,
1.22 x 1450 / 2.25 = 786 mL/min; the printed 766.89 corresponds to a mouse
CLH of 1.19 mL/min. The model files do not use this number.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Remainder-flow leak kept as printed.** Tables 1 and 2 compute the remainder
  flow as cardiac output minus every other flow including the gut, while Eq. 4
  routes the gut outflow through the liver. The arterial blood therefore loses
  Q_Gu x C_A (1.5 mL/min in the mouse, 1100 mL/min in the human) that never
  returns. Figure 2 could be read as giving the hepatic-artery flow the label
  Q_Li, which would conserve mass, but Eq. 4 explicitly uses Q_Li - Q_Gu.
  The mass-conserving alternative cannot clear the mouse dose within 60 min
  and moves the human oral Tmax to about 36 min, so it is not what the authors
  ran. The packaged models follow the equations.
* **Residual gap to the published curves.** In both species the packaged model
  lies at about 0.6-0.9 of the published curves near the peak and about
  0.35-0.65 in the terminal phase, with similar terminal slopes. Discrete alternatives
  (fuT = 1, fuT = fu / P_Li, Vmax per mL of liver) were checked and none closes
  the gap. Figures 3 and 4 are also mutually inconsistent. No parameter was
  adjusted.
* **Unbound fraction in the liver term (fuT).** Eq. 4 uses fuT, defined as the
  fraction unbound in the liver, with liver-water and serum unbound
  concentrations assumed equal; no separate value is printed. The serum value
  (0.76 mouse, 0.54 human) is used. This choice reproduces the paper's own
  well-stirred clearances (1.22 and 477.54 mL/min) exactly.
* **Human renal clearance.** The paper uses only the hepatic CLint for the human
  simulations; CLR is kept at 0 as in the mouse. The paper itself notes that
  hepatic clearance (477.54 mL/min) is well below the observed total clearance
  in humans (1,282.88 mL/min).
* **Human oral input.** Eqs. 9 and 13 send the absorbed oral dose directly into
  the venous blood with ka 0.024 1/min and F 0.16 from a mouse study (the
  dashed lines of Figure 5). The dotted lines of Figure 5 use human oral data
  (F 5.9%) with an unreported ka, so they are not reproduced; the human F can
  be set with `lfdepot = log(0.059)`.
* **Residual error.** The paper fitted all seven mouse profiles with one shared
  variance model, var = (sigma1 + sigma2 x Y)^2. The mouse file attaches it to
  serum (`Cc`, `combined1`); tissue concentrations are returned as
  noise-free outputs (`Cbrain`, `Cmuscle`, `Ckidney`, `Cliver`, `Cgut`,
  `Clung`, plus `Carterial` and `Cother`). The human file is a deterministic
  projection with a zero residual error.
* **No between-animal variability.** The model was fitted to naive-pooled mean
  profiles; no IIV is reported.
* **`cl_renal` not log-transformed.** It is fixed at exactly zero (Table 3),
  which has no log; the convention checker flags it.
* **Body weight.** Organ volumes and flows are fixed at the 30 g mouse and
  70 kg human values of Tables 1 and 2; the paper does not scale them with body
  weight, and neither do the model files.
* **Digitisation.** Published curves in Figures 3-5 were digitised by the
  maintainers from the article figures; points where the curve crosses data
  symbols, tick labels or panel titles were skipped.
